title: range(start, stop): choose where to begin
idea: range(start, stop) counts from start up to (but not including) stop. This lets you print 1..N instead of 0..N-1.

exercises.prompt: What values does range(1, 4) give the loop variable?
exercises.explanation: range(1, 4) starts at 1 and stops before 4: 1, 2, 3. Two numbers: start (included) and stop (excluded).
range(1, 4) is 1, 2, 3. Printing i shows each: 1, 2, 3. The stop value 4 is not included.

exercises.prompt: In range(start, stop), the stop value is NOT included.
exercises.explanation: The loop goes up to but not including stop. range(1, 4) ends at 3, not 4. This is the key rule to remember.

exercises.prompt: To print the numbers 1 to 5, which range do you use?
exercises.explanation: To include 5, stop must be 6 (one past it): range(1, 6) gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Stop is always one beyond the last number.
To end at 4, stop is 5 (one past). range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4.

exercises.prompt: Match each range to the values it produces.
exercises.explanation: Start included, stop excluded. The values run from start up to stop minus one.

exercises.prompt: How many passes does range(3, 7) make?
exercises.explanation: 3, 4, 5, 6 is four values. A handy trick: stop minus start = 7 - 3 = 4 passes.

exercises.prompt: A scoreboard needs to label rounds 1 through 10. Which range?
exercises.explanation: To include 10, stop is 11: range(1, 11) gives 1 through 10. Stop is one past the last label.

exercises.prompt: Common slip: range(1, 5) and you expected it to include 5. What actually prints?
exercises.explanation: Stop is excluded, so 5 is left out. Remember: to reach 5, stop at 6. This off-by-one is worth checking every time.
